documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival 04/04/2024 21:40

Chief complaint: right upper abdominal pain.

HPI: 30 yo F with PCOS, hidradenitis (Hurley II), IBS and history of recurrent UTIs, followed for her IBS and HS, here with 5 hours of severe, waxing and waning RUQ pain that bores through to her back, starting after a big dinner. Nauseated, has not vomited. Bowel movements unchanged, urine normal color.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, nitrofurantoin 100 mg qhs, prenatal vitamin, dicyclomine prn, clindamycin gel. Allergies: NKDA. Former smoker, no EtOH.

Exam: vital signs stable, afebrile. Uncomfortable, shifting on the stretcher. Abdomen: marked RUQ tenderness, no rebound, no guarding; positive Murphy's sign. Lungs clear, heart regular.

Labs: Hgb 12.5, WBC 10.0. T bili 1.2, alk phos 120, AST 40, ALT 45. Amylase 90, lipase 45. Urine hCG negative.

Imaging: RUQ US with multiple gallstones, no cholecystitis.

ED course: IV ketorolac and IV ondansetron with relief; tolerated PO.

Impression: symptomatic cholelithiasis (biliary colic).

Disposition: discharged home. Ondansetron ODT 4 mg q8h prn. Low-fat diet. Follow up with PCP this week to arrange general surgery evaluation; return for fever, jaundice or pain lasting more than a few hours.

Emergency Medicine

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOTE - 10/04/2024

CC: RUQ pain, fever.

30-year-old woman with obesity, PCOS and known gallstones (ED visit in April, surgery not yet arranged) who returns with two days of on-and-off RUQ pain that has steadily worsened, going to the back, with nausea. Fever and shaking chills since yesterday.

Meds: metformin, nitrofurantoin prophylaxis, prenatal vitamin, dicyclomine prn, topical clindamycin. NKDA.

Triage: T 38.9 C, BP 100/60, HR 110, RR 22.
Exam: ill-appearing, jaundiced. RUQ markedly tender, no rebound or guarding. Murphy's sign positive. Lungs clear.

Labs: WBC 15.0, Hgb 12.2, plt 210. Total bilirubin 3.2, direct 2.5, alk phos 190, AST 80, ALT 75. Amylase 90, lipase 45. Urine hCG negative. Blood cultures x2 drawn.

US: multiple gallstones, thickened GB wall, no perforation, CBD dilated.

Assessment: acute cholangitis with gallstones. Fluids, IV piperacillin-tazobactam after cultures. GI consulted for ERCP. Admitted to medicine.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 10/04/2024 from the ED. Discharged 10/08/2024.

Principal diagnosis: acute cholangitis.
Secondary: cholelithiasis; sphincter of Oddi dysfunction (papillary stenosis) s/p biliary sphincterotomy; PCOS; hidradenitis suppurativa; IBS; obesity.

Hospital course: admitted febrile and jaundiced with a dilated common duct. Treated with IV fluids and piperacillin-tazobactam. Blood cultures without growth. ERCP 10/05: cannulation of a tight, stenotic papilla; cholangiogram showed a dilated common bile duct with sludge and several small stones, cleared with balloon sweeps after biliary sphincterotomy. Endoscopist's impression was papillary stenosis (sphincter of Oddi dysfunction) with choledocholithiasis. No post-procedure pancreatitis. Defervesced within 24 hours, pain resolved, diet advanced. Bilirubin 1.3 and alk phos 141 on 10/07.

Discharge medications: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg BID for 5 more days. Resume metformin, nitrofurantoin, prenatal vitamin, dicyclomine prn, topical clindamycin.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week. General surgery for interval laparoscopic cholecystectomy in about 4-6 weeks; referral sent from inpatient team.

Allergies: NKDA.

Hospital Medicine

documents.body:
Seen after discharge 10/8 for gallstone cholangitis.

Finished amoxicillin-clavulanate yesterday. No fever since the hospital, no pain, appetite back, stools and urine normal color. A little tired. Surgery office already called her and she has a consult on 10/28.

Meds reconciled: metformin 1000 BID, nitrofurantoin 100 qhs, prenatal vitamin, dicyclomine prn, clindamycin gel. NKDA.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Sclerae clear, no jaundice. Abdomen soft, no RUQ tenderness. 

A/P:
- Acute cholangitis, treated, clinically resolved. Repeat CMP and CBC today to confirm the liver numbers came down.
- Sphincter of Oddi dysfunction (papillary stenosis) s/p sphincterotomy at ERCP.
- Gallstones, cholecystectomy pending - keep the 10/28 surgery appt.
Return sooner for fever or pain.

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT - 11/18/2024
Preoperative diagnosis: symptomatic cholelithiasis, status post cholangitis and ERCP sphincterotomy.
Postoperative diagnosis: same.
Procedure: laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal.

Findings: gallbladder as expected. Critical view of safety obtained. Cystic duct and artery clipped and divided. Gallbladder removed from the liver bed and extracted in a bag through the umbilical port.
EBL minimal. No complications. Discharged home the same day, tolerating diet. Acetaminophen as needed; no opioids requested.
Pathology: chronic cholecystitis with cholelithiasis.
Follow-up in surgery clinic in 2 weeks.

General Surgery

ED PROVIDER NOTE, 01/16/2026

CC: tired, not eating, dark urine.

32-year-old G1 at 24w4d with history of sphincter of Oddi dysfunction and cholangitis in 2024 (sphincterotomy, then cholecystectomy). About a week of fatigue and poor appetite, and her urine has turned dark. No prior liver disease, no alcohol, no drugs, no recent travel, no sick contacts. First-trimester prenatal screening was unremarkable.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly, prenatal vitamin, dicyclomine prn, clindamycin gel. NKDA.

Exam: afebrile, vitals within normal limits. Scleral icterus. Mild RUQ tenderness. No rash. Gravid abdomen appropriate for dates. Remainder normal.

Labs: total bilirubin 3.2, direct 1.5, AST 850, ALT 920, alk phos 210, total protein 7.1, albumin 4.0. PT 12 sec (control 11). WBC 5.0, Hgb 12.1, platelets 210.

MDM: marked hepatocellular injury in pregnancy with preserved synthetic function. Hepatitis serologies sent. OB evaluated in the ED: fetal heart tones normal. Patient stable for discharge with close hepatology follow-up arranged for next week; return for confusion, bleeding, vomiting, abdominal pain or decreased fetal movement.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Hepatology Consultation
documents.author: hepatology
documents.body:
HEPATOLOGY CONSULTATION - 01/23/2026
Referred from the ED.

32-year-old at 25 weeks with acute hepatocellular injury found 1/16 (AST 850, ALT 920, bilirubin 3.2). Prior biliary history: cholangitis 2024 treated by ERCP sphincterotomy for papillary stenosis, then cholecystectomy. Has taken nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly for UTI prophylaxis continuously for about eight years. No alcohol, supplements other than the prenatal vitamin, or new medicines. Feels somewhat better, urine lighter.

Exam: mild scleral icterus, abdomen gravid and nontender, no stigmata of chronic liver disease.

Serologies from 1/16: hepatitis A IgM, hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis B core IgM and hepatitis C antibody all nonreactive.
Today: AST 312, ALT 405, alk phos 182, total bilirubin 1.6.

Impression: toxic liver disease - drug-induced hepatocellular injury, most likely from long-term nitrofurantoin. Viral hepatitis excluded by serology; already improving.

Plan: stop nitrofurantoin now and do not rechallenge. Do not restart for prophylaxis. Repeat hepatic panel in four weeks. OB aware.

Hepatology

Hepatology follow-up, 02/20/2026, 29 weeks pregnant.

Off nitrofurantoin since 1/23. Energy and appetite back, urine normal color, no itching.

AST 44, ALT 61, alk phos 150 (placental contribution expected), total bilirubin 0.8.

Impression: nitrofurantoin-associated liver injury, resolving.
Plan: OB to repeat a hepatic panel at delivery admission. No further hepatology visits needed unless that is abnormal. Avoid nitrofurantoin in future; please add to her intolerance list.

OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 05/01/2026 in spontaneous labor at 39w4d. Discharged 05/03/2026.

Antepartum course: PCOS on metformin. Asymptomatic bacteriuria at 10 weeks, treated, test of cure negative. Drug-induced liver injury at 24 weeks attributed to nitrofurantoin, which was stopped; resolved by 29 weeks. Tdap given in the third trimester.

Admission labs: hepatic panel and CBC within normal limits.

Delivery: uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery on 05/01/2026 of a healthy infant. Mother and baby recovered routinely.

Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin, metformin 1000 mg BID, acetaminophen as needed.
Intolerance: nitrofurantoin (liver injury).
Follow-up: postpartum visit with OB in 6 weeks; PCP for ongoing care.

Obstetrics & Gynecology
